speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had a fever and altered mental status for two days; can you tell me if you've experienced any seizures, headaches, or neck stiffness? Also, have you noticed any confusion about your surroundings or trouble speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since you are taking haloperidol and have a history of tics, could you clarify if this fever and confusion started before or after you began the medication? Additionally, have you noticed any new skin rash, joint pain, or difficulty moving your limbs?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Liver_Function_Tests, CBC_with_Diff.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The presence of fever, altered mental status, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is classic for NMS, not migraine. I am requesting immediate results from your Complete Blood Count and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel to confirm muscle breakdown and organ function.
